tool_args.old_string:
SmolVLA's pixel-shuffle connector applies $4{\times}4$ spatial folding, concatenating 16 contiguous patches into each token's channel dimension. Each token encodes a non-overlapping $4{\times}4$ receptive field with no redundancy in remaining tokens. SmolVLA collapses to 0.0\% SR at $k{=}0.95$ (removing 6 of 128 tokens) across all four LIBERO suites and both pruning methods, verified on two independent checkpoints (our LoRA reproduction at 44.8\% baseline and the official checkpoint at 59.2\%). The cliff is architectural, not a training artifact.

The collapse is method-independent: all tokens carry spatially entangled information from non-overlapping grids, so no scoring function can identify dispensable tokens. The failure is not which tokens are removed but that any removal breaks the spatial completeness the LLM requires.
